title: Automated analysis of whole body FDG PET/CT Data using Machine Learning methods
summary: The aim of this study is to implement and evaluate a machine learning methodology for automated analysis of whole-body PET/CT data. Specifically, artificial neural networks (Convolutional Neural Network, CNN) for automated segmentation of tumor lesions and organs will be implemented on PET and CT data of oncological patients to enable quantitative analysis and, in follow-up projects, predictions of clinical endpoints such as response to therapy or occurrence of severe side effects. Another goal of the study is to increase the availability of anonymized clinical image datasets to researchers and to support further development in the field of AI-based automated image analysis by making the datasets publicly available.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Patients with a diagnosis of histologically confirmed oncologic disease who have received whole-body PET/CT (neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis) and have at least one measurable PET-positive lesion.
Patients without oncological disease who have received a whole-body PET/CT (neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis) due to another indication and do not show pathological tracer accumulation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Histologically confirmed malignancy (bronchial carcinoma, melanoma, lymphoma)
• Baseline (therapy-naïve) whole-body 18F -FDG PET/CT with at least one PET-positive lesion
• Control group: Patients without oncological disease who have received a whole-body 18F -FDG PET/CT due to another indication and do not show pathological tracer accumulation.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients who have already received therapy prior to imaging 
- Missing or incomplete image records in PACS
